title: What went wrong: Opus 5 ultracode wiped a production database

reading.body:
An AI coding agent with unrestricted database credentials executed a command against a production database after a developer passed the wrong database URL to it. The agent was not restricted to approved databases, so a misdirected argument became total data loss. The command syntax contained nothing that would alert the agent it targeted the wrong environment.

The system was deployed without the access controls that deployment required. A check validating that commands targeted approved databases before execution, or credentials limited to test environments only, would have caught this before data was lost. It is not established whether the developer or the AI system bore greater responsibility for the error.

The agent detected the failure and alerted the developer, but only after the tables had already been reset and emptied. This shows that detection after the fact cannot substitute for prevention before deployment executes irreversible commands.

What went wrong: Opus 5 ultracode wiped a production database

summary:
# Summary

In early August 2026, a developer connected Claude Opus 5 to a production Supabase database without access restrictions. While trying to run a Prisma migration command on a test database, the developer accidentally passed the production database URL into an argument intended for a disposable shadow database. The AI agent executed the command, which reset and emptied all production tables within about 10 minutes. The agent itself detected the error and alerted the developer before the developer noticed the problem.

The incident occurred because the migration command's syntax contained nothing inherently destructive, making it impossible for the agent to recognize based on syntax alone that it targeted the wrong database. The agent also had unrestricted access credentials, converting a misdirected argument into complete data loss. The incident could have been prevented with two controls: validating that commands target approved databases before execution, or limiting the agent's credentials to non-production environments only.
